# Adjudication Task — Chapter 552

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃552화
  2|

  5|띠링.
  6|
  7|
  8|
  9|- [동기화]를 시작합니다. 10, 9, 8, 7…… 1, 0.
 10|
 11|- [동기화]가 성공적으로 완료되었습니다. 증가한 능력치가 신체에 적용되며, 특정 칭호에 한하여 사용이 제한됩니다.
 12|
 13|- [로그아웃]을 완료했습니다.
 14|
 15|
 16|
 17|검게 물들었던 시야가 또렷해지기도 전에, 매번 그랬듯 시원한 바람이 전신을 스쳤다.
 18|
 19|아니, 씻어 내리며 정화(淨化)한다.
 20|
 21|‘동기화.’
 22|
 23|처음 무림과 현실을 오가게 된 이후, 빠짐없이 거쳤던 과정 중 하나다.
 24|
 25|능력치의 변동은 즉각 반영되며 흉터나 상처 따위는 전승되지 않는다.
 26|
 27|체격과 외모의 급격한 변화는 다른 이로 하여금 의구심을 품게 만들어서인지, 서서히 그리고 자연스럽게 변화하는 친절한 기능도 있었다.
 28|
 29|솨아아아.
 30|
 31|이번에도 마찬가지다.
 32|
 33|이미 인간의 한계를 뛰어넘은 신체에 다시 한번 힘이 깃들고, 근육이 유연해지는 것이 느껴진다.
 34|
 35|수신룡과의 전투와 문경의 가르침을 겪으며 다듬어진 공력 역시 예외는 아니었다.
 36|
 37|“후우.”
 38|
 39|가장 먼저 눈에 들어온 것은 먼지 하나 묻지 않은 천장이다.
 40|
 41|수 미터에 이르는 높은 층고(層高)를 둔 천장에는 고풍스러운 그림이 그려져 있었다.
 42|
 43|‘오랜만에 봐서 그런가. 아니면 아직 익숙하지가 않아서 그런가.’
 44|
 45|장강의 지류를 타고 호북성을 향할 때가 마지막이었으니, 대략 두어 달이 흐른 뒤에야 돌아온 셈이다.
 46|
 47|그래서일까, 주위의 모든 것이 낯설다.
 48|
 49|푹신한 이불의 감촉을 느끼며 한참을 천장만 바라보던 나는 문득 입을 열었다.
 50|
 51|“저 그림, 제목이 뭐였죠?”
 52|
 53|나직한 대답이 들려왔다.
 54|
 55|“본 제목은 시스티나 천장화인데, 국내에는 천지창조(The Genesis)로 더 잘 알려져 있습니다. 르네상스 시대의 조각가이자 화가인 미켈란젤로 부오나로티가 탄생시킨 걸작이죠.”
 56|
 57|“아, 미켈란젤로. 그랬었지.”
 58|
 59|“들어 보셨습니까?”
 60|
 61|“워낙 유명하잖아요. 지금 내신 7등급이라고 무시하는 겁니까?”
 62|
 63|“내신 성적이야 무슨 상관이겠습니까. 지금은 진태경 씨가 저 그림보다 훨씬 유명해지셨는데.”
 64|
 65|사박.
 66|
 67|부드러운 가죽 슬리퍼가 대리석을 밟았다.
 68|
 69|베개에 반쯤 파묻힌 얼굴을 옆으로 기울이자, 드넓다 못해 광활한 공간을 가로지르는 한 사람의 모습이 시야에 들어왔다.
 70|
 71|‘어떻게 저 인간은 볼 때마다 잘생겨지냐.’
 72|
 73|어지간해야 질투심이라도 생기지, 일정 수준을 넘어가면 감탄하는 마음만 들기 마련이다.
 74|
 75|더군다나 그런 외모가 자연스럽게 느껴질 정도의 분위기까지 갖추고 있다면 더더욱.
 76|
 77|나는 두 달 만에 마주하는 그를 향해 씩 웃어 보였다.
 78|
 79|“오랜만이네요. 최 팀장님.”
 80|
 81|내가 건넨 인사에 실크 가운을 걸친 미남자, 최 팀장의 발걸음이 우뚝 멈췄다.
 82|
 83|“꼭 멀리 떠났다가 돌아온 사람처럼 말씀하시는군요.”
 84|
 85|“꽤 먼 곳에 있는 꿈을 꿨거든요. 그것도 아주 길게.”
 86|
 87|자그마치 두 달을 넘게 무림에 머물렀으니, 내가 한 말은 결코 거짓이 아니다.
 88|
 89|사실 그간 일어난 사건들을 생각하면 두 달이라는 시간도 짧게 느껴질 정도였다.
 90|
 91|“나쁘지 않은 꿈이었나 보군요.”
 92|
 93|“아뇨. 시작부터 용이랑 싸우는 바람에 그다지.”
 94|
 95|“드래곤 말입니까?”
 96|
 97|“음. 조금 다르긴 한데, 비슷해요.”
 98|
 99|“악몽이네요. 그럴 때는 빨리 잠에서 깨는 게 낫습니다.”
100|
101|달칵.
102|
103|손에 든 커피잔을 침대 옆 탁자에 내려놓은 최 팀장이 말했다.
104|
105|“드십시오.”
106|
107|“엄청나게 비싼 원두커피, 뭐 그런 겁니까?”
108|
109|지난번처럼 무슨 고양이 똥인지, 혁무진 똥인지로 만든 커피라면 극구 사양인데.
110|
111|의심 어린 눈빛으로 커피잔을 노려보던 나는, 문득 콧속 깊숙이 파고드는 익숙한 향에 눈을 크게 떴다.
112|
113|“어라?”
114|
115|설마 하는 표정으로 바라보니 최 팀장이 피식 웃는다.
116|
117|“믹스입니다. 그것도 골드. 진하게.”
118|
119|“키야. 우리 최 팀장님, 뭘 좀 아시네.”
120|
121|“적어도 진태경 씨와 원두커피가 잘 어울리지 않는 조합이라는 것 정도는 알죠.”
122|
123|“굿. 그리핀도르에 십 점 추가.”
124|
125|엄지를 치켜세워 준 나는 단숨에 커피를 들이켰다.
126|
127|음. 역시 이거지. 싸구려지만 달짝지근한 맛.
128|
129|간만에 위대한 현대 문물을 접하니 좀 살 것 같다.
130|
131|“어우, 좋다. 이거 마시니까 정신이 좀 돌아오네요.”
132|
133|“그렇습니까? 하긴, 오늘따라 평소보다 길게 주무시는 것 같더군요.”
134|
135|여타의 각성자나 무림인들도 마찬가지지만, 이미 한계를 뛰어넘은 육체의 소유자인 나는 특히나 잠이 적다.
136|
137|기껏 잔다고 해 봐야 하루에 두 시간을 넘지 않고, 그마저도 수면욕을 채우기 위한 자기만족성 수면이라 할 수 있었다.
138|
139|‘육체를 어지간히 혹사하거나 정신이 피로하지 않는 이상은 문제없지.’
140|
141|그런 놈이 몇 시간씩 죽은 듯이 자면 없던 의심도 생기기 마련이다.
142|
143|나는 하품을 쩍쩍 내뱉으며 기지개를 켰다.
144|
145|“괜찮으십니까?”
146|
147|“가끔 이런 날이 있더라고요. 피곤함이 한 번에 몰려와서 그런가.”
148|
149|비적비적 상반신을 일으킨 나는 손을 뻗었다.
150|
151|침대 옆에 놓인 탁자 위, 허공섭물(虛空攝物)로 끌어당긴 스마트폰이 자석처럼 손아귀에 착 감긴다.
152|
153|‘이것도 오랜만이라 그런가, 되게 이상하게 느껴지네.’
154|
155|매번 현실로 돌아올 때마다 겪는 괴리감 중 하나.
156|
157|내가 어색하게 화면을 톡톡 두드리자 현재 시각이 떴다.
158|
159|am 07:05.
160|
161|오전 일곱 시라. 분명 자정이 지나고 얼마 안 있어 자리에 누웠으니, 얼추 일곱 시간 정도 잔 셈…….
162|
163|“응?”
164|
165|이게 뭐지. 날짜가 이상한데.
166|
167|스마트폰의 화면을 빤히 바라보던 나는, 문득 뇌리를 스치는 생각에 눈을 크게 떴다.
168|
169|“아.”
170|
171|워낙 많은 일들을 겪는 바람에 잊고 있었다.
172|
173|오늘이 무슨 날인지. 왜 내가 굳이 자정이 지난 후에야 방으로 돌아왔는지.
174|
175|그리고 섬광 같은 깨달음이 찾아온 순간, 최 팀장의 목소리가 귓가를 파고들었다.
176|
177|“어젯밤에도 말했지만, 한 번 더 말씀드려야겠군요.”
178|
179|스윽.
180|
181|불쑥 내밀어진 손과 함께, 나직한 목소리가 이어졌다.
182|
183|“올 한 해도 잘 부탁드립니다. 진태경 씨.”
184|
185|2047년 1월 1일.
186|
187|맞다. 오늘은 현대의 새로운 해가 밝은 날이다. 그리고…….
188|
189|“생일 축하합니다.”
190|
191|“……!”
192|
193|바로 나, 진태경의 스물여덟 번째 생일이기도 하다.
194|
195|‘젠장. 벌써?’
196|
197|코앞까지 들이닥친 서른이라는 숫자에 눈앞이 캄캄해진 그때, 저 멀리서 요란한 소리와 함께 두 사람이 들이닥쳤다.
198|
199|“어이! 스물여덟! 엄마가 미역국 먹으래!”
200|
201|“네놈의 탄생일을 치하하노라!”
202|
203|정정한다. 저것들은 사람이 아니라 괴물 두 마리다.
204|
205|오랜만에 마주하는 원수 같은 호적 메이트, 하연이 그리고 그 옆에 있는 금발의 외국인, 스켈레톤 킹(Skeleton King).
206|
207|두 사람의 모습에 나는 한숨을 푹 내쉬었다.
208|
209|
210|
211|* * *
212|
213|
214|
215|무림과 현대의 시간 격차는 어마어마하다.
216|
217|지금까지 알게 된 사실에 의하면 어느 한쪽 세상으로 넘어가는 순간 다른 곳의 시간은 매우 더디게 흘러가는데, 무림의 열흘이 현대의 한 시간인 수준이니 때때로 괴리감을 느끼는 것도 무리는 아니었다.
218|
219|‘특히 이번에는 워낙 많은 일이 있었고.’
220|
221|무림에서도, 현대에서도 급격한 변화가 일어났다.
222|
223|그리고 그 변화 중에는 현재 내가 머무르고 있는 이 대저택 역시 포함되어 있었다.
224|
225|저벅, 저벅.
226|
227|걷는 곳마다 새하얀 대리석이 번쩍이고, 고풍스러운 그림이며 조각상이 가득하다.
228|
229|그리고 무엇보다…….
230|
231|“와, 진짜 더럽게 넓네.”
232|
233|넓다. 그것도 입이 떡 벌어질 만큼.
234|
235|지금까지 내가 두 세상을 오가며 숙소로 썼던 모든 곳을 합쳐도 이 대저택의 규모에 비하면 새 발의 피라고 할 수 있을 정도다.
236|
237|하지만 정작 대저택의 주인은 그렇게 생각하지 않는 듯 했다.
238|
239|“진태경 씨 말씀대로 조금 큰 편이긴 합니다. 손도 많이 가고요.”
240|
241|최 팀장의 말에, 뒤에서 졸졸 따라오던 하연이가 불쑥 입을 열었다.
242|
243|“손이 많이 가는 것 치고는 다른 분들이 안 보이던데요. 맞죠, 아저씨?”
244|
245|최 팀장을 부르는 호칭이 아니다.
246|
247|순금을 녹여 만든 것 같은 금발과 신비로운 빛을 띤 금안(金眼).
248|
249|얼핏 보면 할리우드에서 염문깨나 뿌릴 것처럼 생긴 외국인이 얼굴을 찡그렸다.
250|
251|“설마 이 몸을 부른 건 아니겠지.”
252|
253|하연이가 숨도 쉬지 않고 대답했다.
254|
255|“맞는데요.”
256|
257|“허.”
258|
259|헛웃음을 지은 외국인, 매직 존슨의 환영 마법 덕분에 인간의 모습으로 재탄생한 스켈레톤 킹이 피식 웃었다.
260|
261|“뭔가 잘못 알고 있는 모양이군. 이 몸이 알기로 이 나라의 아저씨란 윗 항렬의 친척 남성. 혹은 중년층 남성을 이르는 단어인데.”
262|
263|“네.”
264|
265|“…….”
266|
267|잠시 말문이 막혀 있던 스켈레톤 킹이 목소리를 쥐어 짜냈다.
268|
269|“그러니까 내 말은…….”
270|
271|“서른 살 넘으셨다면서요. 그럼 저한테는 아저씨 맞아요.”
272|
273|“아니, 넘긴 했는데…….”
274|
275|“아하. 알겠어요. 그러니까 아저씨인데, 아저씨라고 불리기는 싫으신 거 맞죠?”
276|
277|“……!”
278|
279|금빛 눈동자가 파르르 떨렸다. 발걸음도 멈춘 채 하연이를 노려보던 스켈레톤 킹이 중얼거렸다.
280|
281|“핏줄은 닮는다던데. 확실히 남매가 맞군.”
282|
283|나와 하연이가 동시에 대답했다.
284|
285|“나 외동이다.”
286|
287|“저 외동인데요, 아저씨.”
288|
289|세상에, 간악한 인간이 둘로 늘어나다니.
290|
291|딱 그렇게 쓰여 있는 눈동자로 나와 하연이를 번갈아 본 녀석이 포기한 표정으로 고개를 내저었다.
292|
293|“알았다. 알았으니까 둘 다 그만해라. 그리고 너, 건방진 인간 계집아. 이 몸을 두 번 다시 아저씨 따위로 불렀다가는…….”
294|
295|저벅.
296|
297|스켈레톤 킹의 말은 이어지지 못했다.
298|
299|어느새 하연이가 발걸음도 멈춘 채 멍한 눈동자로 녀석을 바라보고 있었기 때문이다.
300|
301|“뭐라……고요?”
302|
303|“아니. 그게 아니고. 내가 말실수를 했다.”
304|
305|스켈레톤 킹은 내 눈치를 보며 수습하기에 바빴고, 최 팀장은 드디어 올 게 왔다는 표정으로 한숨을 내쉬었다.
306|
307|“기어코 일을 저질렀군요. 저자는 제가 데려갈 테니 진태경 씨는 동생분을 잘 다독여 주십시오. 오해 안 하도록 조심하시고요.”
308|
309|“……?”
310|
311|무슨 소리야, 이게.
312|
313|나는 최 팀장을 보며 눈을 깜빡였다.
314|
315|“왜요?”
316|
317|“네?”
318|

“The official title is the Sistine Chapel ceiling frescoes, but in Korea they’re better known as *The Creation*—*The Genesis*. They’re a masterpiece by Michelangelo Buonarroti, a Renaissance sculptor and painter.”

[P19]
“Ah, Michelangelo. Right.”

[P20]
“You’ve heard of him?”

[P21]
“He’s famous. Are you looking down on me because my school grades were Level 7?”

[P22]
“What do your school grades have to do with it? You’re much more famous than that painting now, Mr. Jin Taekyung.”

[P23]
*Tap.*

[P24]
Soft leather slippers met the marble floor.

[P25]
I turned my head on the pillow and saw a man crossing the vast—no, practically boundless—room.

[P26]
*How does he get more handsome every time I see him?*

[P27]
If he were merely good-looking, I might have been jealous. But once someone passed a certain point, all I could do was admire him. Especially when he had the presence to make those looks seem perfectly natural.

[P28]
I grinned at the man I was seeing for the first time in two months.

[P29]
“It’s been a while, Team Leader Choi.”

[P30]
Team Leader Choi, handsome as ever in a silk robe, stopped in his tracks.

[P31]
“You say that as though you’ve come back from somewhere far away.”

[P32]
“I dreamed about a pretty distant place. It was a long dream, too.”

[P33]
I’d spent more than two months in Murim, so it wasn’t a lie. Considering everything that had happened, two months almost felt too short.

[P34]
“It must have been a good dream.”

[P35]
“Not really. I had to fight a dragon right at the start.”

[P36]
“A dragon?”

[P37]
“Something a little different, but close.”

[P38]
“A nightmare, then. Better to wake up quickly from one of those.”

[P39]
*Clink.*

[P40]
Team Leader Choi set the cup he was holding on the bedside table.

[P41]
“Have some coffee.”

[P42]
“Is this made from some incredibly expensive beans?”

[P43]
If it was coffee made from cat shit—or Hyuk Mujin’s shit—like last time, I was going to refuse.

[P44]
I eyed the cup suspiciously. Then a familiar aroma reached me, and my eyes widened.

[P45]
“Huh?”

[P46]
I looked up at him. Team Leader Choi gave a quiet laugh.

[P47]
“It’s instant. Gold. Made strong.”

[P48]
“Damn, Team Leader Choi. You know what’s good.”

[P49]
“At least I know you and coffee brewed from beans aren’t a good match.”

[P50]
“Good. Ten points to Gryffindor.”

[P51]
I gave him a thumbs-up and downed the coffee in one gulp.

[P52]
*Mm. That’s the stuff.*

[P53]
Cheap and sweet. Getting a taste of modern civilization again made me feel alive.

[P54]
“Ah, that’s good. I’m starting to wake up.”

[P55]
“Are you? You did sleep longer than usual today.”

[P56]
Like other Awakened and Murim martial artists, I had a body that had surpassed human limits. I needed even less sleep than most.

[P57]
I rarely slept more than two hours a day, and even that was more to satisfy the desire to sleep than out of any real need.

[P58]
*Unless I’ve pushed my body too hard or worn myself out mentally, I’m fine.*

[P59]
So when someone like me slept like the dead for hours, people were bound to wonder why.

[P60]
I yawned and stretched.

[P61]
“Are you all right?” he asked.

[P62]
“I get days like this sometimes. Maybe all the fatigue caught up with me at once.”

[P63]
I sat up groggily and reached out. The smartphone on the bedside table flew toward me through *Seizing an Object Through Empty Space* and snapped into my hand like a magnet.

[P64]
*Maybe it’s because I haven’t used one in a while, but this feels really strange.*

[P65]
It was part of the disorientation I felt every time I returned to reality.

[P66]
I tapped the screen awkwardly. The time appeared.

[P67]
**7:05 a.m.**

[P68]
Seven in the morning. I’d gone to bed not long after midnight, so I’d slept about seven hours…

[P69]
“Hm?”

[P70]
Wait. The date was wrong.

[P71]
I stared at the screen until a thought struck me.

[P72]
“Ah.”

[P73]
So much had happened that I’d forgotten what day it was—and why I’d waited until after midnight to return to my room.

[P74]
Just as I remembered, Team Leader Choi spoke.

[P75]
“I said this last night, but I suppose I should say it again.”

[P76]
*Swish.*

[P77]
He held out his hand.

[P78]
“I look forward to working with you this year as well, Mr. Jin Taekyung.”

[P79]
January 1, 2047.

[P80]
Right. It was the first day of a new year in the modern world. And…

[P81]
“Happy birthday.”

[P82]
“…!”

[P83]
It was also my twenty-eighth birthday.

[P84]
*Damn it. Already?*

[P85]
The number thirty loomed so close that my vision went dark. Then two people burst in from across the room, making a racket.

[P86]
“Hey, Twenty-Eight! Mom says to come eat seaweed soup!”[^1]

[P87]
“I congratulate you upon the day of your birth!”

[P88]
I take it back. They weren’t people. They were two monsters.

[P89]
One was Hayeon, my old enemy on the family register, whom I hadn’t seen in ages. The other was the blond foreigner beside her: the Skeleton King.

[P90]
I sighed at the sight of them.

[P91]
* * *

[P92]
The time difference between Murim and the modern world was enormous.

[P93]
From what I’d learned, whenever I crossed into one world, time in the other slowed to a crawl. Ten days in Murim amounted to about an hour in the modern world. No wonder I sometimes felt out of step.

[P94]
*Especially this time. So much happened.*

[P95]
Both worlds had changed rapidly. One of the changes was the enormous mansion where I now lived.

[P96]
*Step. Step.*

[P97]
White marble gleamed beneath our feet, and old-fashioned paintings and statues filled the halls.

[P98]
More than anything, though…

[P99]
“Wow. This place is ridiculously huge.”

[P100]
Huge enough to leave me speechless. Even if I put together every place I’d stayed while traveling between the two worlds, the total would be nothing next to this mansion.

[P101]
Its owner didn’t seem to agree.

[P102]
“As you said, Mr. Jin Taekyung, it is somewhat large. It also takes a lot of work to maintain.”

[P103]
“For a place that takes so much work, I don’t see anyone else around. Right, old man?”

[P104]
Hayeon, who’d been trailing behind us, had suddenly joined the conversation.

[P105]
She wasn’t talking to Team Leader Choi.

[P106]
The foreigner with hair like molten gold and strangely gleaming golden eyes frowned. At a glance, he looked like the sort of man who’d be caught up in Hollywood dating scandals.

[P107]
“Surely you don’t mean me.”

[P108]
“I do.”

[P109]
“Hah.”

[P110]
The Skeleton King—given a human appearance by Magic Johnson’s illusion magic—let out a short laugh.

[P111]
“You seem to misunderstand. As I understand it, the term you used refers to a male relative of an older generation, or a middle-aged man.”

[P112]
“Yes.”

[P113]
“…”

[P114]
For a moment, the Skeleton King was at a loss for words.

[P115]
“What I mean is…”

[P116]
“You said you’re over thirty. That makes you an old man to me.”

[P117]
“I am over thirty, but…”

[P118]
“Oh, I get it. You *are* an old man. You just don’t want to be called one, right?”

[P119]
“…!”

[P120]
His golden eyes trembled. He stopped walking and glared at Hayeon.

[P121]
“They say blood relatives resemble each other. You two really are siblings.”

[P122]
Hayeon and I answered together.

[P123]
“I’m an only child.”

[P124]
“I’m an only child, old man.”

[P125]
*Good heavens. Now there were two wicked humans.*

[P126]
That was written all over his face as he looked from one of us to the other. Finally, he shook his head in defeat.

[P127]
“All right. Just stop it, both of you. And you, insolent human girl—if you ever call me an old man again…”

[P128]
*Step.*

[P129]
He never finished.

[P130]
Hayeon had stopped walking. She was staring at him blankly.

[P131]
“What… did you call me?”

[P132]
“No. That isn’t what I meant. I misspoke.”

[P133]
The Skeleton King scrambled to take it back, glancing at me. Team Leader Choi sighed as though he’d been expecting this to happen sooner or later.

[P134]
“You’ve done it now. I’ll take him away, Mr. Jin Taekyung. Please calm your sister down, and be careful she doesn’t misunderstand.”

[P135]
“…?”

[P136]
What was he talking about?

[P137]
I blinked at him.

[P138]
“Why?”

[P139]
“Pardon?”

[P140]
“Why would I need to calm her down?”

[P141]
“Why? Miss Hayeon was just insulted—”

[P142]
Before he could finish, Hayeon spoke.

[P143]
“‘Insolent human girl’? Is that something you say to a person, you long-nosed bastard?”

[P144]
“…Huh?”

[P145]
“…What?”

[P146]
Here we go. I smiled warmly.

[P147]
*She hasn’t changed a bit.*

[P148]
Yes. This was Jin Hayeon.

[P149]
My capillaries swelled with pride. At last, I truly felt like I’d returned to the modern world.

[P150]
Hayeon whipped around to face me.

[P151]
“Did you hear what that Yankee bastard just said?”

[P152]
I nodded solemnly.

[P153]
“I heard.”

[P154]
“Does he have dirt on you? Did someone catch you doing a private webcam show? Why else would you hang around with a bastard like that? Someone who isn’t even human…”

[P155]
*That’s surprisingly accurate.*

[P156]
“Oh, right,” I said, impressed. “He really isn’t human.”

[P157]
“He called me an insolent human girl. Who the hell says that?”

[P158]
“Well, he said it. It was just a bad thing to say.”

[P159]
“If he’d called me a crazy bitch or something normal, I wouldn’t even complain. But *human girl*? It feels so gross. Seriously.”

[P160]
I took out my smartphone and whispered, “Siri, tell me today’s weather.”

[P161]
—Today’s weather is clear.

[P162]
“You asshole. You think I’m in the mood for wordplay? Your one and only little sister just got called that by someone else!”

[P163]
I hurriedly straightened my clothes and bowed politely.

[P164]
“Hello. My name is Jin Taekyung, and I’m an only child.”

[P165]
“You really are a lunatic.”

[P166]
“That’s rather harsh for a first meeting. I’ll sue you for defamation by stating facts.”

[P167]
Hayeon’s eyes turned cold.

[P168]
“I’m telling Mom everything.”

[P169]
“What?”

[P170]
“I’m telling Mom. Every last thing.”

[P171]
“Are you threatening me?”

[P172]
“Yep.”

[P173]
“You little…”

[P174]
*Wham!*

[P175]
Eyes bulging, I grabbed a collar with all my strength.

[P176]
Not Hayeon’s, of course. The Skeleton King’s.

[P177]
“Apologize to my sister right now! You less-than-human bastard! You monster!”

[P178]
“I-I’m sorry! I was wrong! I’ll apologize a hundred times, just please…!”

[P179]
“Of course she’s insolent! And human! And a girl! But you can’t put all three together like that!”

[P180]
“Ugh! Grrrgh!”

[P181]
“Say it properly! Put the right words together!”

[P182]
“I-Insolent! Person! Girl!”

[P183]
*Boom.*

[P184]
At least, I thought I heard something like that.

[P185]
It was Hayeon’s anger gauge bursting. She picked up the nearest plaster statue.

[P186]
“Die. Just die, both of you!”

[P187]
*Whoosh! Clang!*

[P188]
One clang a day was enough to turn the hallway into chaos.

[P189]
Hayeon charged at us like a valiant Viking warrior. Team Leader Choi stared at the scene in disbelief.

[P190]
That was when—

[P191]
“I told you to come eat. What’s all this noise…!”

[P192]
The elevator at the far end of the hallway opened. A familiar face emerged and froze.

[P193]
Dear Lady Kim Jeonghee.

[P194]
My mother.

[P195]
“…What are you two doing?”

[P196]
From her tiny body—not even 160 centimeters tall—I felt an aura to rival at least one of the Ten Kings.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
